concept.th-network.def: The wires and wireless links that let one program talk to another, even across the world.
concept.th-client.def: The program that asks for something over a network.
concept.th-server.def: The program that answers requests over a network.
concept.th-request.def: A message a client sends asking for something.
concept.th-response.def: The answer a server sends back.
concept.th-api.def: The set list of things a server offers and how to ask for them - like a menu.
concept.th-internet.def: The giant network of networks that joins millions of separate networks into one, so a program can reach another almost anywhere.
concept.th-ip-address.def: The number that identifies a machine on the internet, so a request knows where to go - like 142.250.1.14.
concept.th-dns.def: The system that looks up the IP address behind a name like example.com, like a phone book turning a name into a number.
concept.th-http.def: The shared set of rules the web follows for writing a request and a response - for example a GET request and a 200 OK response.
